observation.visible_scene: An elevated/aerial view of a city skyline at a low sun (sunrise or sunset). A large body of water covered by a flat layer of fog/mist sits behind the buildings, with the sun glowing near the horizon. Silhouetted skyscrapers cluster on the right, lower buildings and rooftops fill the foreground, and thin wispy plus brighter cumulus clouds spread across the sky. A narrow plume of smoke/steam rises from a point on the far shore near the center of the frame.
visible_changes: The smoke/steam plume is present and continuously rising from the first to the last frame; it is an ongoing emission, not a start or stop within the excerpt.
The upper portion of the plume changes shape over the segment: the top billows and leans/bends progressively toward the right compared with its more vertical, thinner appearance in the early frames.

The city buildings, the fog layer, the horizon line, and the sun's position keep the same location relative to the frame edges throughout, indicating no pan, tilt, or zoom (camera essentially static).

The cloud formations (wispy streaks on the left, bright mass on the right, and the diagonal streak in the upper-right sky) show no clearly discernible movement or deformation across the ~2.7 s window; they appear effectively static.
outside_clip_unknowns: What emits the plume (stack, ship, fire, etc.) is not visible.
Whether the plume's drift continues, dissipates, or changes direction after the last frame is unknown.
The rate of any longer-term sky/sun/cloud evolution beyond this short crop is unknown.
uncertain_details: The apparent rightward bending of the plume top is subtle and could partly reflect compression rather than true wind drift.
Any very slow cloud drift or micro-camera motion cannot be confirmed from these frames.
The diagonal streak in the upper-right sky is treated as a static cloud/contrail feature; its nature is not verifiable.
